operation: Independent source/assertion audit; no changes applied.
scope: Current v2 root browser runner, compared with canonical REVIEW-E2E definitions.

findings.evidence: Runner holds request before service dispatch and calls renewal.fetch only after refresh expiry. Canonical case requires provider success before expiry and delayed response delivery after expiry.
findings.consequence: Expired-provider rejection cannot verify late successful response delivery.
findings.next_action: Retain this expired-dispatch variant separately. Obtain successful response before expiry, hold it, then fulfill after browser deadline for canonical late-delivery variant.

findings.evidence: Only opaque authorization substitution exists. Missing-iat variant and valid local-provider retry are absent. Route does not first assert upstream HTTP200 and usable authorization.
findings.consequence: Canonical case is incomplete; upstream failure could exercise ordinary error handling instead of candidate access validation.
findings.next_action: Confirm upstream success, run missing-iat variant, then remove substitution and assert valid retry installs returned access, closes prompt, validates against BFF.

findings.evidence: Home is mounted from login while access is fresh. Runner waits until twenty seconds remain without remount or token update. It explicitly discloses missing near-expiry registration trigger.
findings.consequence: Completed recovery is meaningful control evidence but does not verify no-catch-up boundary for Home registering late.
findings.next_action: Keep control labeled; cause supported Home mount or token/expiry update with usable refresh and <25s access, capture request counts and complete renewal.

findings.evidence: Only replacement login status200 is asserted. Runner states completion inside one-second Logout delay but captures no exact click/start/callback identity or installed B access hash. Additional logout request count is recorded only as raw events, not asserted.
findings.consequence: Stale dialog state could be observed, but required race ordering and no-op button claims need explicit evidence reconciliation.
findings.next_action: Capture Logout click wall time, replacement response/install time and B hash; require replacement before callback deadline; assert B retained and zero additional logout calls after second click.

findings.evidence: Both logins use same fixture credentials. observe() omits sub/sessionId and request refresh hash. impact label correctly says NO_CROSS_USER_PROOF.
findings.consequence: Retained old refresh with new access can be observed; identity switch cannot be established.
findings.next_action: Limit claim to old-refresh retention unless separate authorized users and correlation hashes are available.

findings.evidence: Promise.allSettled return values are discarded. mkdir/context creation occur outside run try/finally. Such failures leave no results row.
findings.consequence: Summary can silently omit a requested case after an early setup exception.
findings.next_action: Reconcile requested case-side inventory to results and retain rejected setup tasks explicitly.

accepted_limits: Synthetic response mutation, malformed refresh signature and same-user direct setter are disclosed.
REVIEW05 observes bounded pending recovery; it does not claim indefinite suspension.
COMPLETED is an execution disposition and does not itself establish canonical predicates passed.
